**Proposed mechanism:** TYMP (HGNC:11852) —DISRUPTS→ Pyrimidine salvage pathway (REACT:R-HSA-1908298); Pyrimidine salvage pathway (REACT:R-HSA-1908298) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); DPYD (HGNC:2767) —DISRUPTS→ Uracil (CHEBI:27337); Uracil (CHEBI:27337) —LEADS_TO→ Developmental delay (HP:0001263). Loss-of-function mutations in TYMP impair the pyrimidine salvage pathway, leading to intellectual disability. Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in DPYD impair the same pathway, leading to accumulation of uracil and developmental delay. The shared pathway implicates a common module.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of mutations in TYMP and DPYD in individuals presenting with the core phenotypes of both diseases, or identification of distinct molecular pathways not involving pyrimidine metabolism that explain the phenotypes. _(variant: High frequency of pathogenic variants in TYMP or DPYD in gnomAD for the respective populations that do not correlate with disease penetrance.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared reliance on the pyrimidine salvage pathway highlights potential therapeutic strategies. For example, interventions aimed at restoring pyrimidine homeostasis or mitigating the downstream effects of its dysregulation could be beneficial for both conditions.

#### 2. mitochondrial DNA depletion syndrome, myopathic form  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.417)

**Why it matters:** Targeting mitochondrial nucleotide metabolism or improving mitochondrial ATP synthesis could be potential therapeutic strategies for both MONDO:0011283 and MONDO:0012301.

#### 4. hereditary arterial and articular multiple calcification syndrome  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.397)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-73621)

**Proposed mechanism:** NT5E (HGNC:18525) —DECREASES→ Adenosine (CHEBI:17537); Adenosine (CHEBI:17537) —DECREASES→ Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198); Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Arterial calcification (HP:0002712); TYMP (HGNC:12067) —DISRUPTS→ Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198); Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Articular calcification (HP:0030044). Loss of function in NT5E (disease B) leads to increased extracellular adenosine, which in turn negatively impacts extracellular matrix organization, contributing to arterial calcification. Loss of function in TYMP (disease A) directly disrupts extracellular matrix organization, leading to articular calcification. Both pathways converge on the extracellular matrix organization pathway.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of a pathogenic variant in NT5E or TYMP with a minor allele frequency > 0.01 in gnomAD would falsify the claim that these variants are the sole cause of the respective diseases. _(variant: rs71007525)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared pathway of extracellular matrix dysregulation in both diseases could lead to the development of novel therapeutic strategies targeting matrix integrity or adenosine signaling for both arterial and articular calcification.
